videos.title: Alan Ayckbourn: The Plays in Facts (2025)
videos.description:
A slideshow of 20 facts about Alan Ayckbourn's plays from 1959 to the present day, updated for 2025.

Researched and written by Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Alan Ayckbourn: A Life in Facts (2025)
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn: A Life In Facts (2025 edition) is a short slide show setting out key moments and achievements in the life and career of the playwright and director Alan Ayckbourn.

It is researched and written by Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A., drawing on resources at the playwright's official website www.alanayckbourn.net.

The video has been updated for 2025 to include the latest facts & figures relating to the playwright.

Researched, written & narrated by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by Bensound (https://www.bensound.com)

videos.title: The Ayckbourn Collection at Scarborough Museums & Galleries
videos.description:
In August 2023, it was announced The Ayckbourn Collection had been donated to Scarborough Museums & Galleries. A small collection of significant items relating to Alan Ayckbourn, his mentor Stephen Joseph, theatre in the round and their contribution to Scarborough's cultural heritage and history.

Join Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A. - who curated the Collection and facilitated the donation - as he introduces the collection, why it was created and how it came to Scarborough Museums & Galleries.

Items from The Ayckbourn Collection will also be going on displays at Scarborough Art Gallery from 16 September.

Written, researched & presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A. With thanks to Scarborough Museums & Galleries and The Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York.

A SiMo production in association with Haydonning Ltd.

videos.title: Ayckbourn's Gardens: A Talk with Simon Murgatroyd
videos.description:
On 11 July 2023, Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist Simon Murgatroyd M.A. gave a talk about gardens in Alan Ayckbourn's plays. Over the course of 45 minutes, he explored why the playwright chooses to use garden spaces as well as how the illusion of a garden can be created in theatre in the round as well as exploring how Alan Ayckbourn uses gardens both as real spaces and liminal spaces.

The talk took place in there Italian Gardens on Scarborough's South Cliff and was arranged in conjunction with Gemma Alexander, the South Cliff Gardens Community Engagement Officer.

To find out about future talks with Simon, visit http://events.theatre-in-the-round.co.uk.

videos.title: The Norman Conquests at 50
videos.description:
2023 marks the 50th anniversary of Alan Ayckbourn's beloved play trilogy The Norman Conquests.

To mark the event, his archivist - Simon Murgatroyd - presents a look at the history of the trilogy from its premiere in Scarborough in 1973 to its Tony Award Winning revival in New York in 2009.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

A SiMo production for @AlanAyckbournPlaywright in association with Haydonning Ltd and the Borthwick Institute for Archives.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: A Round Town: Theatre in the Round in Scarborough
videos.description:
On 9 June 2023, a new website - A Round Town - is being launched to celebrate the contribution of theatre in the round to the cultural heritage and history of the town of Scarborough.

Curated and created by Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist Simon Murgatroyd M.A., www.theatre-in-the-round.co.uk, looks at the history of theatre in the round from 1955 to 2009 (its creation to the stepping down of Alan Ayckbourn as Artistic Director), its venues, the plays, people involved and its impact on Scarborough.

This video introduces and launches the website, offering a glimpse into some of the stories and subjects explored in almost a 1,000 pages on the website.

It is presented and written by Simon Murgatroyd, creator of the new website and creator of Alan Ayckbourn's Official Website www.alanayckbourn.net.

With thanks to Scarborough Theatre Trust, Tony Bartholomew, Adrian Gatie and Haydonning Ltd.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com).

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: The Withdrawn Plays
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, returns with another edition of Ask The Archivist.

Here he answers the question, which Ayckbourn plays have been withdrawn and why?

Find out which nine of the playwright's 89 plays (as of 2023) have been withdrawn and where you can actually find them.

If you have an Ayckbourn question for Simon, email it to him at enquiries@alanayckbourn.net or add it to the comment box.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A. A SiMo production in association with Haydonning Ltd.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com).

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn: The Family Plays
videos.description:
Between 1988 and 2004, the playwright Alan Ayckbourn wrote almost a dozen of what he dubs his 'family' plays. From Mr A's Amazing Maze Plays to Miss Yesterday, these plays were written to encourage families to experience theatre together.

SpotLight on Ayckbourn charts the development of these plays and the author's increasing move toward family plays which encompass similar themes and demands on his audiences as the adult plays to the point where the line dividing the two is almost invisible.

To the playwright's mind, the family plays are of as much significance in his body of work as his 'adult' work, the two often complementing each other. Here his Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, charts the development of these plays and why they are so significant to his playwriting canon.

Written and narrated by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

A SiMo production in association with Haydonning Ltd and the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York.

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: When did The Norman Conquests become The Norman Conquests?
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, is back to answer your questions about the playwright and his plays.

For this Ask The Archivist, Simon answers the question of when The Norman Conquests trilogy actually became known as The Norman Conquests - the plays did not have this title for their world premiere production in 1973.

Find out this and what the right order to see the trilogy is in this video.

Written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn: The Early Christmas Plays
videos.description:
Early in his career, the playwright Alan Ayckbourn wrote two children's plays for Christmas, Dad's Tale and Christmas V Mastermind. He now considers them the 'black sheep' of his play canon!

The playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, goes back to 1960 and 1962 to shed some light on these two plays which were never produced again, never published and have long since been withdrawn.

Discover the story of Alan's first - and only - attempt to write ballets and what is probably the only play ever written about industrial action in Santa's workshop.

Obscure and long forgotten, this is the story of Alan Ayckbourn's early Christmas plays.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A. A SiMo production in association with Haydonning Ltd.

Royalty free-music by BenSound (www.bensound.com).

videos.title: Portholes in Time - Scarborough Sea Wall Heritage Trail
videos.description:
Own 6 December 2022, Sir Alan Ayckbourn inaugurated Scarborough's Sea Wall Heritage Trail with its 31 'portholes' offering a glimpse at the history and heritage of the seaside resort.

The video looks at the Heritage Trail and includes exclusive footage of Sir Alan launching the trail at the inauguration event.

With thanks to Scarborough Maritime Heritage Centre for inviting Simon Murgatroyd, Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, to the event.

Filmed, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com).

A SiMo production in association with Haydonning Ltd.

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn: The Supernatural Plays
videos.description:
There's a chilling presence in this SpotLight on Ayckbourn as the playwright's Archivist turns his attention to Alan Ayckbourn's supernatural plays.

Exploring his three supernatural works as well as other more obscure short works, Simon Murgatroyd, looks at the various plays and other works from 1975 to the present which feature spectres and the unexplained.

From What The Devil! to A Cut in the Rates, Taking Steps to The Fearsome Threesome, Haunting Julia to Snake in the Grass and Life & Beth to Roundelay, Simon looks at how the supernatural pervades a significant section of the playwright's work.

It also includes an exclusive extract from Alan Ayckbourn's audio recording of Haunting Julia.

Researched, written & presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

A SiMo production in association with Haydonning Ltd.

videos.title: Rewriting History:  Discovering The Abandoned Absurd Person Singular Manuscript
videos.description:
In 2022, Alan Ayckbourn's seminal play Absurd Person Singular celebrated its 50th anniversary.

That same year, an extraordinary discovery by the playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A. and the Borthwick Institute for Archives rewrote our understanding of how the play was conceived and developed.

The discovery of the long-thought lost abandoned first draft of the play revealed a play initially completely unlike that which we know today and which differed considerably from what the playwright's accounts of what he wrote. It paints the development of the play in an entirely new light.

This video, hosted by Simon Murgatroyd, looks into the discovery, its significance as well as what else was discovered alongside new acquisitions relating to the popular play which redefine our understanding of the play and its path to becoming one of the key British plays of late 20th century British theatre.

Written, presented and researched by Simon Murgatroyd M.A. A SiMo production in association with the Borthwick Institute for Archives.

Learn more at the newly launched website www.absurdpersonsingular.com.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: How Many Multi-Part Plays Has Alan Ayckbourn Written?
videos.description:
Ask The Archivist returns with Simon Murgatroyd responding to your questions about Alan Ayckbourn and his plays.

This time, there's the question of how many multi-part plays Alan Ayckbourn has written from trilogies to duologies to other works in more than one part.

Researched and presented by the playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Produced by Simon in association with Haydonning Ltd.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn - A Chorus of Disapproval (pt.3): The Film
videos.description:
A Chorus of Disapproval is one of Alan Ayckbourn's most popular and performed works. It was also his first play to be adapted into a film.

In 1988, Michael Winner adapted the play for the big screen, filming in the playwright's home-town of Scarborough, producing what the playwright considers to be a travesty of his play.

SpotLight on Ayckbourn explores the background to the film, how and why Alan agreed to let Winner tackle it, how it was adapted and folded as well as looking at  the aftermath of the movie.

Drawing extensively on correspondence held in The Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York, the video offers a never before seen glimpse behind the scenes of one of the single greatest disappointments of Alan Ayckbourn's long career.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

A SiMo production in association with Haydonning Ltd and the Borthwick Institute for Archives.

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn - A Chorus of Disapproval (pt.2): The National Theatre & the West End
videos.description:
SpotLight on Ayckbourn continues its looks at one of Alan Ayckbourn's most successful and popular works with part 2 of its look at A Chorus of Disapproval.

Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, tells the story of the less than smooth transition of the play from Scarborough to the National Theatre and its particular casting issues.

From there, he explores a contentious transfer into the West End which  marked the final stage role of the actor Colin Blakely.

Using material exclusively drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive at the Borthwick Institute for Archives, SpotLight on Ayckbourn sheds new light on a previously little known aspect of A Chorus of Disapproval's journey.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com).

A SiMo & Haydonning Ltd production in association with the Borthwick Institute for Archives.

videos.title: Absurd Person Singular - In Facts
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, narrates an illustrated 10 facts about the playwright's acclaimed and successful play.

Researched, written and narrated by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Illustrated with material drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive at the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Absurd Person Singular at 50: The World Premiere Production
videos.description:
The Ayckbourn YouTube Channel kicks off its 50th anniversary celebrations of Alan Ayckbourn's seminal play, Absurd Person Singular, with a look at the world premiere production in 1972.

Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, narrates this pictorial history of the first production of the play at the Library Theatre, Scarborough, which opened on 26 June 1972.

Illustrated by photographs and publicity material drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive at the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York, the video offers a glimpse at some rarely seen material relating to the production.

A selection of publicity images from all three acts of the play are also presented, many on display for the first time since 1972.

Written, research and narrated by Simon Murgatroyd.

With thanks to the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn - A Chorus Of Disapproval (pt.1): Writing the Play
videos.description:
The creation of one of Alan Ayckbourn's most popular works, A Chorus of Disapproval, comes under the spotlight in the first of three videos about the play.

Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, looks into the background to and writing of A Chorus of Disapproval, examine how the playwright's original plans for the play were nothing like what he actually wrote.

With material drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive held at the Northwick Institute for Archives at the University of York, Simon explores the journey of the play from conception to completion as well as discovering the staging of the original production was unique and has never been replicated since.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

With thanks to the Northwick Institute for Archives.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

Find out more about Alan Ayckbourn and his plays at www.alanayckbourn.net and Simon Murgatroyd at www.simon-murgatroyd.com

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: What is the Most Performed Ayckbourn Play?
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, is back to answer the latest question sent via enquiries@alanayckbourn.net.

He tackles the question of 'what is Alan Ayckbourn's most performed play?' The answer may well surprise you!

Don't forget you can send your questions to Simon either via the comment box or by emailing enquiries@alanayckbourn.net.

Written, presented & edited by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: Who Is The Most Prolific Ayckbourn Actor?
videos.description:
Ask The Archivist sees Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, answering questions about the playwright and his plays.

Who has appeared in the most Ayckbourn productions in Scarborough? is the question under the spotlight as Simon looks at the playwright's adopted hometown where he has premiered the vast majority of his plays.

He reveals the actors who have appeared in the most world premieres of Alan Ayckbourn's plays as well as who is the most prolific actor.

Don't forget to send your own questions either by emailing enquiries@alanayckbourn.net or by typing them in the comments box.

Researched and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn: Just Between Ourselves
videos.description:
SpotLight on Ayckbourn goes behind the scenes of the playwright Alan Ayckbourn's most significant works.

His Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A., look at the creation of his 1976 tragi-comedy Just Between Ourselves and how the playwright came to write it - with early notes showing the play could have been even darker than it was.

The video also includes contemporary audio interviews with Alan Ayckbourn talking about the play as well as previously unseen material and photographs held in the Ayckbourn Archive at the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York.

This is a fascinating glimpse into one of Alan Ayckbourn's most significant and praised plays.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

With thanks to the Borthwick Institute of Archives at the University of York.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: What is Michael Gambon's Connection to Alan Ayckbourn?
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, looks at the long and successful professional relationship between the actor Michael Gambon and the playwright Alan Ayckbourn, which has won the actor three Olivier Awards.

If you have a question for Ask The Archivist, email Simon at enquiries@alanayckbourn.net or ask them in the comments box.

Written, research and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: Has Alan Ayckbourn Written For Television or Film?
videos.description:
Ask The Archivist sees Simon Murgatroyd answering the question of whether Alan Ayckbourn has written any screenplays for television or film and whether they have been produced.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn - The Norman Conquests (pt.3): The TV Adaptation
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's classic trilogy comes under the SpotLight again in the final part of a series looking at key moments in the history of The Norman Conquests.

This time, Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist - Simon Murgatroyd M.A. - looks at the 1977 television adaptation of The Norman Conquests. This extraordinarily successful adaptation has been seen more times than any other single production of the playwright's work and continues to be popular more than forty years on.

Simon Murgatroyd explores the behind-the-scenes negotiations which went into making the television adaptation, the disputes over running times, the desire to make a spin-off television series and how the playwright reacted to the idea of television adaptations of his plays.

The video features exclusive material drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive at the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York.

Researched, written & presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Alan Ayckbourn - A Life in Theatre: The National Theatre
videos.description:
The Life in Theatre series concludes with a look at Alan Ayckbourn's long and significant relationship with the National Theatre.

Simon Murgatroyd is joined by Sir Alan Ayckbourn  in telling the story of playwright's relationship with the National from 1977 to the present day. From Bedroom Farce to Way Upstream, A Small Family Business to his acclaimed production of A View From The Bridge, this tells the story of Alan's five decades working with the theatre.

The video features exclusive interview recordings with Sir Alan Ayckbourn as well as rarely seen photographs and images drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive at the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York.

Researched, written and presented by Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A. with additional material by Sir Alan Ayckbourn.

Special thanks to the National Theatre.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn - The Norman Conquests (pt.2): The West End
videos.description:
The Norman Conquests in the West End continues SpotLight on Ayckbourn's trilogy of videos looking at the background to and creation of one of the playwright's most famed works.

Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, looks into the Ayckbourn Archive to explore the convoluted journey of The Norman Conquests trilogy from Scarborough to the West End. The difficulties which led to it being first produced at an interim theatre and the reluctance of anyone to produce a trilogy in London.

With photos and documents drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive, the video offers a look at what eventually became one of Alan Ayckbourn's most notable West End successes.

Researched, written & presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: How Many Plays Has Alan Ayckbourn Written? (2022 edition)
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, answers his most frequently asked question, how many plays has Sir Alan Ayckbourn actually written?

Bearing in mind this will almost certainly have changed by 2023 (!), Simon gives Sir Alan's definitive answer for 2022 as well as looking at why other sources have it wrong.

Written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty-free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn: Absent Friends
videos.description:
SpotLight on Ayckbourn: Absent Friends looks at the inspiration and development behind Alan Ayckbourn's acclaimed 1974 play, Absent Friends.

The playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, tells the story of how the play was inspired by both the playwright experiences with The Norman Conquests and a personal experience from his own life to write the play.

The author's handwritten notes held in the Ayckbourn Archive at the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York illustrate how the play changed and developed during its conception. Finally, the video looks at the extraordinary speed at which the play was written and produced. 

Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, presents the video with quotes from the playwright, production and publicity photos as well as other exclusive archive material.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn - The Norman Conquests (pt.1): Writing the Trilogy
videos.description:
SpotLight on Ayckbourn: The Norman Conquests delves into the Ayckbourn Archive to explore how Alan Ayckbourn's award-winning trilogy, The Norman Conquests, came to be written.

Featuring audio commentary and insights from Alan Ayckbourn himself, the video looks at the unlikely series of events which led to the trilogy, its inspiration as well as the challenges of writing three interconnected plays despite financial and practical limitations.

Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, presents the video with audio and quotes from the playwright, production and publicity photos as well as other exclusive archive material in this insight into how one of the playwright's most significant works came to be written.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ayckbourn InSights: The Christmas Plays
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn is known for several plays set at Christmas such as Season's Greetings and Absurd Person Singular.

But did you know that Christmas appears far more regularly in his plays than you might realise? The playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, looks at just how many of the playwright's works are set at Christmas and why Alan Ayckbourn thinks it's the perfect time to set a play.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn: How The Other Half Loves
videos.description:
SpotLight on Ayckbourn: How The Other Half Loves looks at the creation and writing of Alan Ayckbourn's ninth play, How The Other Half Loves.

From his inspiration living in a council flat in Leeds to unexpected alterations due to injuries to actors to unwelcome input from a famed West End star, this video traces how the play was written and developed.

Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, presents the video with quotes from the playwright, production photos and other material in this insight into how one of the playwright's most popular and successful works came about.

Researched, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: Which Ayckbourn plays haven't premiered in Scarborough?
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, answers a new question to the playwright's YouTube channel...

Which Alan Ayckbourn plays haven't premiere in his adopted home town of Scarborough?

Simon looks back from 1959 to the present day to answer the question as the playwright prepares to open his 86th play - All Lies - at The Old Laundry Theatre, Bowness-on-Windermere, on 6 May 2022.

Research, written & presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: Have Alan Ayckbourn's Plays Been Translated into Other Languages?
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A., answers more questions about Alan Ayckbourn's plays, here looking at the translations of his writing into other languages.

Written, edited & presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.
Principal photography by Mo Murgatroyd
Filmed at Portmeirion, Wales.

Royalty Free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn: Relatively Speaking
videos.description:
SpotLight on Ayckbourn goes behind-the-scenes to look at the background to and creation of some of Alan Ayckbourn's most significant works.

Spotlight on Ayckbourn: Relatively Speaking looks at the playwright's breakout work which is one of his most popular and produced plays. It looks at how the impetus to create one of his most successful works was instigated as a result of one of his biggest failures. It explores the process of writing the play and how the initial production was unlike anything which followed.

Never before seen pages from the director's prompt script reveal how he cut reams of material from the play without the playwright's knowledge for the world premiere production.

From there, the video looks at how the West End production altered the play including completely changing its climax and a bizarre decision to amend the first scene.

Researched and presented by Simon Murgatroyd, this is a fascinating insight into how Alan Ayckbourn wrote this pivotal play in his writing career.

Original manuscript pages kindly reproduced courtesy of Dr Paul Elsam (© Haydonning Ltd).

Researched, presented and edited by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ask The Archivist: What is the earliest piece of Ayckbourn writing?
videos.description:
Simon Murgatroyd M.A., Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, is back with another question for Ask The Archivist.

What is the earliest know piece of Ayckbourn writing? sees Simon look back to both Alan's youth at prep school and his earliest professional days in theatre to find his earliest known writing, his first published work and his first play.

If you have a question about Alan Ayckbourn and his plays, send it to enquiries@alanayckbourn.net - Simon will try and answer any question and the best will be used in future videos.

Presented and researched by Simon Murgatroyd.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Alan Ayckbourn - A Life in Theatre: BBC Radio Drama Producer
videos.description:
The majority of Alan Ayckbourn's life and career has been spent in the theatre as playwright, writer and Artistic Director.
However, in 1964, his experiences with his first West End transfer led him to consider abandoning his theatrical ambitions and he took a job at the BBC in Leeds as an Assistant Radio Drama Producer.
He worked there for five years for the renowned producer Alfred Bradley, the driving force behind the Northern writing explosion of the period.
Arguably, Alan learnt vital skills whilst at the BBC which would enable him to successfully return to theatre and take on the role of Artistic Director of the Library Theatre on 1972.
This narrated video by Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, looks at these rarely explored five years of the playwright's life alongside quotes from the playwright as well as exclusive images drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive at the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York. 

Written, researched, edited and narrated by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music from Bensound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Unseen Ayckbourn: Clue the Movie
videos.description:
Did you know Alan Ayckbourn was approached in 1981 to write the screenplay for the movie Clue, based on the popular boardgame?

In a new series of videos looking at the more obscure projects Alan Ayckbourn has worked on, the playwright's Archivist - Simon Murgatroyd - tells the story of how Alan Ayckbourn was approached by a Hollywood Studio to adapt the boardgame, but which would ultimately fall through whilst, arguably, leading the playwright to create his own take on the material several years later.

Researched, written & presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ask The Archivist - What was the First Ayckbourn Play to be Adapted for Television?
videos.description:
Ask The Archivist sees Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist answering questions about the playwright and his plays.

What was the First Ayckbourn Play to be Adapted for TV? gets to the bottom of what the first TV adaptation was and when it was broadcast. Since 1967, more than 25 of the playwright's works have been adapted for the screen, can you guess which was the first?

Written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Ayckbourn: Mr Whatnot (updated)
videos.description:
SpotLight on Ayckbourn puts Alan Ayckbourn's sixth play, Mr Whatnot, under the spotlight. The playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, narrates the background and creation of the play which was the first of his plays to transfer to the West End and is directly responsible for him writing his breakout hit, Relatively Speaking. Largely ignored within the Ayckbourn play canon, Mr Whatnot is a fascinating and idiosyncratic creation unlike anything else the playwright has ever written.

The video includes exclusive and rarely seen images from the Ayckbourn Archive held at the Borthwick Institute for Archives at the University of York.

Researched, written & narrated by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Amended and updated: 3 September 2021

videos.description:
Ask the Archivist with Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A., looks at the question who Roland Allen was in relation to Alan Ayckbourn's early writing.

Written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

videos.title: Ayckbourn InSights: What Inspired Alan Ayckbourn to Write The Norman Conquests?
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd M.A.,reveals just why Alan Ayckbourn was inspired to write one of his most famous works, The Norman Conquests trilogy. At a time when trilogies were regarded as box office death, Alan wrote what would become one of the most celebrated of his works - for a regional theatre which would have struggled to survive had it  been a box office flop. But as to what inspired Alan Ayckbourn, the answer lies in an innocent question posed with unexpected consequences....

Research, written and presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.co.uk)

videos.title: An Interview with Alan Ayckbourn: Remembering The Blitz
videos.description:
In an exclusive interview for the Ayckbourn YouTube channel, playwright Alan Ayckbourn talks to his Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, about his memories of growing up during the Blitz during World War 2. These memories would help inspire his 85th play, The Girl Next Door.

Interview by and copyright of Simon Murgatroyd. Editing by Simon Murgatroyd.

Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com).

videos.title: The Birth of the Library Theatre: 14 July 1955
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist looks back to the opening night of the Library Theatre in Scarborough - the forerunner of the Stephen Joseph Theatre today - on 14 July 1955, to see what it would have been like to attend the first night of the debut of the UK's first professional theatre-in-the-round company. From Stephen Joseph and Alan Ayckbourn's descriptions of the space to audience reactions to the debut play, the video offers a fascinating insight into the origins of a company which continues to thrive today and has found fame around the UK and the world.

Researched, written & presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.
Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Alan Ayckbourn - A Life in Theatre: The Artistic Director
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn is best known as playwright and director but for 37 years of his life, he was the Artistic Director of the Stephen Joseph Theatre in Scarborough.
The playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, narrates this guide through this career from 1972 when he took on the role at the then Library Theatre through to his retirement in 2009 from the company's present home, the Stephen Joseph Theatre.
It explores why he took on the role, how it affected profoundly affected both his career and the theatre itself as well as asking what he brought to the company and how, ultimately, it not only ensured the SJT's survival but preserved the legacy of its founder and his most significant mentor, Stephen Joseph.

Written, researched, edited and narrated by Simon Murgatroyd.
Royalty free music from Bensound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Ayckbourn InSights - Why Absurd Person Singular?
videos.description:
A new series of short videos offering insights into some of Alan Ayckbourn's most famous plays kicks off with the perennial question, why is Absurd Person Singular called Absurd Person Singular? And what does the title of the play mean? Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, offers a brief insight into this frequently asked question.

Researched & presented by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.
Royalty from music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Stephen Joseph - Alan Ayckbourn's Inspiration
videos.description:
On the centennial of theatre pioneer Stephen Joseph's birth on 13 June 1921, his impact and influence on Alan Ayckbourn is explored.
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, delves into why Stephen Joseph is so significant to understanding Alan Ayckbourn and how he became one of the UK's most successful modern playwrights.
Alan met Stephen Joseph in 1957 and Stephen encouraged Alan to both write and direct and was a father figure to the young man. After his death in 1967, Alan would take over the Library Theatre which Stephen had founded in Scarborough in 1957 and would run it for the next 37 years.
Stephen Joseph is inarguably the single most influential figure in Alan Ayckbourn's life and this video demonstrates why.

Written, researched and edited by Simon Murgatroyd M.A.
Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Archiving for Alan Ayckbourn - International Archives Day
videos.description:
To mark International Archives Day (9 June), Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist - Simon Murgatroyd - talks about his role as Archivist and what it means to him. From talking about his work in the archive to running the playwright's official website, Simon also talks about why he holds archiving close to his heart and how he feels it contributes to theatre culture.

Presented by Simon Murgatroyd.
Royalty free music by BenSound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Alan Ayckbourn - A Life In Theatre: The Director
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's career as a director from 1961 to the present day is explored as the playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, narrates a guide to what Alan Ayckbourn considers to be his main theatrical career.
Ayckbourn began directing at the Library Theatre, Scarborough, in 1961 encouraged by Stephen Joseph and would go on to become a pre-eminent theatre-in-the-round director. He has directed more than 350 productions during his life including more than 40 productions in the West End or at the National Theatre.
This video takes a comprehensive look at his directing career which is as equally important as his writing career over the past six decades.
It includes quotes from the playwright himself alongside an extensive range of images drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive.

Written, researched, edited and narrated by Simon Murgatroyd.
Royalty free music from Bensound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: Alan Ayckbourn - A Life in Theatre: The Playwright
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's career as a playwright from 1959 to the present day is explored as the playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, narrates a guide to the theatre career he is most well-known for in this ongoing series looking at his entire life in theatre.
From Ayckbourn's early initial plays at the Library Theatre, Scarborough, through to his West End successes through to the possibilities enabled by being Artistic Director of the Stephen Joseph Theatre for 37 years, the video takes a comprehensive look at the career which has come to define Alan Ayckbourn and for which he is best known for more than six decades and over 80 plays.
It includes quotes from the playwright himself alongside an extensive range of images drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive.

Written, researched, edited and narrated by Simon Murgatroyd.
Royalty free music from Bensound (www.bensound.com)

videos.title: SpotLight on Alan Ayckbourn: Standing Room Only
videos.description:
My look at some of Alan Ayckbourn's most significant plays - both famous and not so well known - continues with his fourth play, Standing Room Only. Drawing on material from the Ayckbourn Archive and the British Library, we look at why this play is so significant - not least for the number of 'firsts' in the playwright's early career and how the West End and TV beckoned and why it's so important to his directing career.

Researched, written & narrated by Simon Murgatroyd - Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist.

videos.title: Alan Ayckbourn: A Life In Theatre - The Actor
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's career as an actor from 1957 to 1964 is explored as the playwright's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, narrates a guide to his formative theatre career in the first of a series looking at his entire theatre career.
Ayckbourn's initial professional career as an actor comes under the spotlight. From acting with Donald Wolfit to working at venues such as the Connaught Theatre, Oxford Theatre Club and the Library Theatre, Scarborough, to the acting role which, ironically, led to him becoming a playwright, the video takes an extensive look at the playwright's acting career alongside quotes from the playwright himself and extensive images drawn from the Ayckbourn Archive.

Researched and narrated by Simon Murgatroyd.
Royalty free music from Bensound (www.bensound.co.uk)

videos.title: Spotlight on Ayckbourn: The Square Cat
videos.description:
Alan Ayckbourn's Archivist, Simon Murgatroyd, kicks off a new series of videos looking at the creation and history behind some of the playwright's most significant works. SpotLight on Ayckbourn: The Square Cat looks at Ayckbourn's first play, drawing on material held in the Ayckbourn Archive including an original manuscript. Learn about how and why Alan Ayckbourn wrote his first play and a surprising element in its creation in the shape of Harold Pinter.
Research, written & narrated by Simon Murgatroyd.
